sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Immunofluorescence (IF) in transfected cells: wild-type V5-tagged C3ORF52 localises along the cell membrane (surface_only). Functional assay of the tagged protein not reported.
sites.rationale: C3orf52 is a single-pass Type II membrane protein (N-in, C-out); the only extracellular terminus is the C-terminus at residue 217. Python confirmed seq[216]='E' and seq[86]='L' (last TM residue), placing the C-terminus 130 residues from the TM boundary — well beyond the ≥3-residue requirement. Because the ledger names no specific residue for the tag junction but the topology leaves exactly one extracellular terminus, position_evidence is topology_derived and insert_after_residue is set to 217. L2 independently confirms the tagged construct reaches the plasma membrane. L1 (PMC7405639): full-length C3ORF52 cDNA with a C-terminal V5-tag cloned into pcDNA3.1 and expressed in mammalian cells. L2 (same paper) confirms the V5-tagged wild-type protein localises to the cell membrane by immunofluorescence. No residue number is stated for the tag junction; however, the protein has exactly one extracellular terminus — the C-terminus at residue 217 — because the N-terminus (1–66) is intracellular and the single TM helix (67–87) leaves the C-terminal domain (88–217) extracellular. The junction is therefore unambiguously after residue 217.

sources.claim: A synthetic C3ORF52 ( NM_024616.2 ) complementary DNA (cDNA) construct with a C-terminal V5-tag and a synthetic LIPH ( NM_139248.3 ) cDNA with a C-terminal HA-tag were cloned into pcDNA3.1 plasmids (Epoch Life Science, USA).

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are available, both from PMC7405639. L1 establishes the C-terminal V5-tagged full-length construct; L2 confirms surface localisation and additionally reports that the p.Tyr164Ter truncation variant causes ER retention, recorded in other_positions. No internal extracellular loop insertion is supported by the ledger. The N-terminus (residues 1–66) is intracellular and therefore not a candidate for a surface tag. No intracellular tag sites are reported in the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: p.Tyr164Ter truncation causes ER retention (colocalisation with PDI) and decreased expression, indicating that the C-terminal region from Y164 onward is required for proper folding and trafficking to the plasma membrane.
